prompt: Increment an AtomicInteger and a plain int side by side, then hammer them from four joined threads and watch only one of them stay exact. Complete record, safeCount and hammer.
explanation: unsafeHits++ is three separate steps -- read, add one, write back -- so two threads can read the same value and one increment simply disappears. AtomicInteger.incrementAndGet() performs the whole read-modify-write as a single hardware-level compare-and-set, which is why the safe count is exactly threads * perThread every run. Joining every worker before reading the counters is what makes the result deterministic and the workers' writes visible to the main thread.
hints: record() needs two lines: safeHits.incrementAndGet() and unsafeHits++ -- do not try to synchronize anything.
In hammer, keep the started threads in a Thread[] so you can loop over the same array again and join() each one.
Start every thread first and only then join them; joining inside the starting loop would run the workers one after another and hide the race entirely.
